name: otp-input
purpose: The field for a one-time code: the six digits an authenticator app shows, or a code sent by email or SMS. It looks like a row of boxes, one character each, but it is **one real text input** laid over the boxes, so the browser's one-time-code autofill (`autocomplete="one-time-code"`), password managers, paste and screen readers all see a single field. Typing fills the next box (auto-advance), Backspace empties the last one, and a pasted code (`123 456`, `123-456`, with a line break) keeps only its valid characters and fills every box. When the last box fills it emits `complete`, so the screen can submit without a button press. It replaces the Console Kit's six `InputText`s with hand-written focus moves (`mfa-setup-block`, `mfa-authenticate-block`).
useWhen: Multi-factor authentication: set-up confirmation and sign-in challenge.
Verifying an email address or a phone number with a short code.
Any short, fixed-length code the user copies from somewhere else.
avoidWhen: A password or a secret of free length → use `PasswordInput`.
A long token or API key → use `Input` with a copy affordance.
A number with a range → use `NumberInput`.
related: field` — wrap it in a `Field` for the label, the description and the error; the label names the input.
password-input` — the other credential input of the auth screens.
input` — the plain text field it shares tokens with.
bestPractices: Label it with what the code is and where it comes from: `Authentication code`, and a description `The 6-digit code from your authenticator app.
Submit on `complete` only when the code is the last thing to fill; keep a Verify button for keyboard users and for a failed attempt.
After a rejected code, mark it `invalid`, clear it, and keep focus in it.
Use `group="3"` for codes people read aloud or copy from a phone; it draws a separator between groups and does not change the value.

props.name: modelValue
props.doc: The code typed so far, without separators.

props.name: length
props.doc: How many characters the code has; one box each.

props.name: mode
props.doc: numeric` keeps digits and opens the number keypad; `alphanumeric` keeps letters and digits, upper case.

props.name: group
props.doc: Draw a separator after every `group` boxes (`3` gives `123 – 456`). `0` draws none.

props.name: disabled
props.doc: Disables the field while a code is being checked.

props.name: invalid
props.doc: Danger borders on every box and `aria-invalid`; set after a rejected code.

props.name: autofocus
props.doc: Focus the field on mount, for a screen whose only task is the code.
